blocks.text: Reserve Adequacy Review: A Briefing on the Work Under Way

Prepared for {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} by Meridian Actuarial Advisors. The engagement opened on {{fact:f:E-2017-001.start}}, and this short briefing sets out what we are doing, who is doing it, and where the work stands now that it is under way.
The Question We Are Here to Answer

items: Whether the reserves {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} carries are adequate to meet the obligations they are meant to fund.
An independent view, formed from your own data as reconciled, not carried in from another engagement.
A written opinion that keeps what the data show, what we assume, and what we conclude as three separate matters.
Reconciling the reserve data you provide against your own financial records, so the figures we test are the figures you carry.
Reviewing the assumptions behind the current reserves, keeping those that regulation fixes apart from those that rest on judgment.
Building an independent estimate of the required reserves and comparing it against the carried figures, with any difference attributed to its sources.
Outside the work: auditing your statements, setting your reserves for you, or opining on your rates.
Jennifer Vasquez, Consulting Actuary, owns the relationship and the judgment calls on scope.
David Sherman, Senior Analyst, builds the valuation workbook and reconciles the data as it arrives.
Megan Dudley, Actuarial Associate, keeps the exhibits, the data checks, and the running request log.
Michelle Hudson, your Director of Operations, is our single point of contact for the data.
We are in the early weeks, and the emphasis now is squarely on the data rather than on conclusions.
The reserve detail has begun to arrive and the reconciliation against your year-end records is under way.
One grouping question on the summary totals is open and being run to ground; we expect it to close without consequence.
We are not offering findings yet, because an opinion this early would run ahead of what the work supports.

blocks.text: From here we finish the reconciliation, then move into the assumption review and the independent estimate, and we will send a short status note as each piece lands so you always know where things stand. The single most useful thing from your side is the assumption documentation as it stood at the valuation date; our one clear next step is to get that itemized request to you this week and confirm each item as it comes back.
